paper_a.title: Right inverses of Levy processes: the excursion measure in the general case

paper_b.title: Phonon excitation and instabilities in biased graphene nanoconstrictions

metadata.description: Registry mismatch: neither input paper concerns the curated topic (Chen-Qin vs Cai-Liu-Xia high-dimensional two-sample mean tests). Paper A (paper119, Savov & Winkel 2010, arXiv:1003.2122) studies the excursion measure away from the right inverse of a Levy process; Paper B (paper120, Gunst et al. 2013, arXiv:1305.5907) is a condensed-matter physics paper on phonon excitation and runaway instabilities in biased graphene nanoconstrictions, computed via DFT-NEGF and a semi-classical generalized Langevin equation. The two papers share no mathematical objects, no common framework, and no overlapping problem statement. Pair is flagged NEG; no Level-1 cross-paper matches are defensible. Per spec, none-entries are emitted for the paper-origin Level-1 nodes of each side to make the alignment file complete.

matches.explanation: Definition of the Laplace exponent rho(q) of the minimal partial right inverse of a Levy process. Paper B contains no Laplace-exponent / subordinator concept; it is a phonon-electron transport paper. No counterpart.
Excursion measure n^Z away from the right inverse on excursion path space. Paper B has no excursion-theoretic objects; mismatch is total.

Killed semi-group P_t^dagger of the Levy process frozen at zero. Paper B's semi-group structure is a phonon Green's function in equation EP120.5; the analogy is at most superficial (both are propagators) and there is no mathematical correspondence between Levy-process killing and phonon-bath damping. Treated as none.
Concatenation operator on càdlàg paths used to build n^Z = tilde-n^R oplus K. No path-space concatenation appears in paper B.
Hitting-time decomposition T_{x} = T_x^+ + tilde T_{-O_x} for Levy processes. Paper B has no hitting-time analysis.
Discretization formula for the Laplace exponent rho(q) via dyadic stopping times. No counterpart in paper B.
Alternative ladder-based construction tilde K(n) of the right inverse. Paper B's only algorithm (AP120.1) is a DFT-NEGF computation of Langevin parameters - completely different domain.

Theorem 1: representation of the excursion measure n^Z as a concatenation of the supremum-excursion measure with the killed kernel. This is the main contribution of paper A and has no analogue in a graphene-phonon paper.
Corollary 2: explicit entrance laws of n^Z. No counterpart in paper B.
Proposition 3: closed-form Laplace exponent rho(q) and characteristics (kappa_K, eta_K, Lambda_K) of the right inverse. No counterpart.
Corollary 4: recurrent Levy processes admit a partial right inverse iff a full right inverse. No counterpart.
Lemma 5: limit of the auxiliary sequence hat z_n. No counterpart.
Lemma 6: limit of the complementary sequence tilde z_n. No counterpart.
Lemma 7: tilde K(n) is a bivariate subordinator with explicit drift and Levy measure. No counterpart.
Lemma 8: identification of K as inf-sup of tilde K(n). No counterpart.
Lemma 9: subsequential a.s. convergence tilde K_x(n_k) -> K_x. No counterpart.
Proof of Lemma 5 (resolvent + DCT argument). Paper B has no proofs of comparable type.
Proof of Lemma 6 via [1, Thm VI.18]. No counterpart.
Proof of Proposition 3 combining Lemmas 5 and 6 with Wiener-Hopf inversion. No counterpart.
Proof of Corollary 4 (recurrent equivalence). No counterpart.
Proof of Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 via entrance-law uniqueness. No counterpart.
Alternative proof of Proposition 3 via approximations from Appendix A. No counterpart.
Proof of Lemma 7 via Poisson thinning. No counterpart.
Proof of Lemma 8 via quasi-left-continuity. No counterpart.
Proof of Lemma 9 (subsequence extraction). No counterpart.
Definition of a graphene nanoconstriction (paper B). No counterpart in paper A.
Mass-scaled ion displacements Q used as the Langevin dynamical variable. No counterpart in paper A.
Inverse quality factor 1/Q with phonon-bath and electronic contributions. No counterpart in paper A.
Runaway-mode definition (negatively damped phonon mode). No counterpart in paper A.
IETS-mode definition. No counterpart in paper A.
Retarded electronic phonon self-energy with Hilbert-transform decomposition into friction, wind, renormalization, and Berry forces. No counterpart in paper A.
Interaction-weighted electron-hole pair density of states Lambda_{alpha beta}. No counterpart in paper A.
Noise spectral density S_f including Joule heating. No counterpart in paper A.

Nonequilibrium retarded phonon Green's function D^r(omega). No counterpart in paper A; the superficial 'propagator' analogy with the killed semi-group P_t^dagger (DP119.8) is too thin to record as analogous.
Average phonon kinetic energy E_kin formula. No counterpart in paper A.
Master equation for phonon number. No counterpart in paper A.
Fermi-golden-rule emission/absorption rates. No counterpart in paper A.
Electronic friction expressed as A - B. No counterpart in paper A.
